properties.decision:
RECORDED AS A FINDING, 2026-08-19. Nothing built, nothing asked for yet.

**A THIRD MEASURED INSTANCE of `req:a-deliberate-state-is-not-a-defect` — and the first one where THE FIX WAS ALREADY SHIPPED.** Instances (a) and (b) on that requirement are from dev_storyflow, 2026-08-04 and 2026-08-15, and `cap:a-ruling-parks-a-node-and-parked-nodes-are-counted` was built to answer them. This instance happened afterwards, in reflow2's OWN repo, with `governed_by(ruling: "parks")` available and served.

**WHAT HAPPENED.** Anthony registered two agent-authored field reports as Artifacts with no claim edges — a deliberate no-claim registration, exactly the genre the requirement describes. Structural defects went **35 → 38** and the BL-199 CI gate turned the PR red. The agent triaged it, argued at length that no honest edge existed (of the five the orphan message names, four are false for a dated field report and DOCUMENTS asserts the file should stay in step with the design, which is backwards for a frozen record), recommended DELETING both Artifact nodes, and did so on Anthony's word (`fbc8e55`). Defects fell to 36. The gate went green.

🛑 **THAT IS THE EXACT FAILURE MODE `req:a-deliberate-state-is-not-a-defect` PREDICTED, QUOTED FROM ITS OWN TEXT:** *"a later seat watching the count climb has an incentive to stop registering documents and leave them absent, which is the worse state."* The prediction came true against an agent that had the remedy in its own tool list and did not reach it.

⭐ **WHY IT WAS NOT REACHED — and this is the whole finding.** `parks` is documented ON THE TOOL (`governed_by`'s parameter hint). A person in this situation is not reading tool hints; they are reading the three messages that told them they had a problem, and NONE of the three names parking:
· `orphan_node`'s text lists the five claim edges, then says *"No mechanical repair. Linking this node to something would assert a relationship nobody drew"* — which reads as **there is nothing you can honestly do**, when in fact there is;
· `tools/self_host_uses_documents.py`'s FAIL text says *"nothing in the graph says what the file is FOR"*, with no hint that *"it is FOR nothing, deliberately"* is a sayable thing;
· the **link-artifacts** skill covers REALIZES / DOCUMENTS / SPECIFIES and stops.

📌 **THE DOCTRINE THIS IS AN INSTANCE OF:** vocabulary reaches a design only with a TYPED TOOL **and** an INSTRUCTION **and** a DETECTOR THAT NOTICES ABSENCE. `parks` has the tool and the detector. The instruction is missing precisely where it would be read. A shipped capability nobody can find at the moment of need is, from the user's side, indistinguishable from one that was never built — and the defect count is what makes that visible.

✅ **IT ALSO CLOSES A BOUND THE REQUIREMENT LEFT OPEN.** That node records as NOT ESTABLISHED: *"whether reflow2's own graph holds any deliberate no-claim registrations — it holds 14 DOCUMENTS-only artifacts, which is a different state and not this one."* As of 2026-08-19 it held exactly two, they were the first, and they were deleted rather than parked before anyone counted them.

**WHAT WOULD FIX THE MISS, cheapest first — text, not mechanism:**
1. `orphan_node`'s `repair_is_a_judgement` names `ruling: parks` as the honest alternative when the node's unattached state may be deliberate. It already contains the sentence *"a parked thought that correctly governs nothing yet"* — it describes the remedy without naming it.
2. The BL-199 gate's FAIL text says the same.
3. **link-artifacts** grows the case: a document that correctly claims nothing is registered and parked, not left bare and not given a false DOCUMENTS.

**FOR A USER'S PROJECT, which is the point rather than the self-host trivia:** any brownfield project carries observations of a system it did not build — incident reports, customer complaints, field trial data, a vendor's test certificate. Each is an Artifact that correctly describes and implements nothing. Today the first thing such a user meets is a defect offering five edges, all false, and a repair note that reads as a dead end. Brookhaven's ~10-year-old bluesky stack is the live case.

🛑 REVERSIBLE, AND IT NEEDS ANTHONY'S WORD: the two reports are still files in `docs/feedback/`, unchanged. Re-registering and parking them requires an ACCEPTED Decision — `parks` refuses a `proposed` ruling by design, so that a musing cannot suppress a finding. The agent cannot give itself that word.

SEPARATE AND STILL OPEN: whether `artifact_type` should gain a value for human evidence (it has `test_result` for the machine kind). Parking says "attaches to nothing on purpose", which is not the same as "this is dated evidence and it ages" — cf. `req:evidence-carries-the-date-it-was-taken`.

⚠️ RECORD-KEEPING NOTE: the first write of this node was MALFORMED — a closing tag and the rationale were sent inside the decision body, so the node briefly carried trailing markup and no `rationale` property. Corrected in place the same session; the prior value survives only in that call's reply.
properties.name: OPEN — `parks` shipped, and an agent with the tool available still deleted the documents instead: the mechanism is named on the TOOL and the person is reading the DEFECT
properties.rationale: Recorded rather than folded into req:a-deliberate-state-is-not-a-defect because it is a different claim about a different failure: that requirement asks the DETECTOR to read a ruling, and it has been answered by cap:a-ruling-parks-a-node-and-parked-nodes-are-counted; this says the answer is not reachable from where the problem is met, which no existing node states. Kept as a finding rather than a proposal because Anthony's standing instruction this session was to capture the feedback and defer the work. Recorded at all because the reasoning behind a wrong recommendation exists nowhere else: commit fbc8e55 argues that no honest edge exists for a dated field report, and it will keep asserting that to every future reader unless something says otherwise. The three named neighbours were read in full before writing, on the dedup guard's refusal, and the guard is the reason this node is a third instance rather than a fourth restatement.
